26	class EchoingStdin:
27	    def __init__(self, input: t.BinaryIO, output: t.BinaryIO) -> None:
28	        self._input = input
29	        self._output = output
30	        self._paused = False

36	        if not self._paused:

42	        return self._echo(self._input.read(n))

227	class CliRunner:
228	    """The CLI runner provides functionality to invoke a Click command line
229	    script for unittesting purposes in a isolated environment.  This only
230	    works in single-threaded systems without any concurrency as it changes the
231	    global interpreter state.
232	
233	    :param charset: the character set for the input and output data.
234	    :param env: a dictionary with environment variables for overriding.
235	    :param echo_stdin: if this is set to `True`, then reading from `<stdin>` writes
236	                       to `<stdout>`.  This is useful for showing examples in
237	                       some circumstances.  Note that regular prompts
238	                       will automatically echo the input.
239	    :param catch_exceptions: Whether to catch any exceptions other than
240	                             ``SystemExit`` when running :meth:`~CliRunner.invoke`.
241	
242	    .. versionchanged:: 8.2
243	        Added the ``catch_exceptions`` parameter.
244	
245	    .. versionchanged:: 8.2
246	        ``mix_stderr`` parameter has been removed.
247	    """
248	
249	    def __init__(
250	        self,
251	        charset: str = "utf-8",
252	        env: cabc.Mapping[str, str | None] | None = None,
253	        echo_stdin: bool = False,
254	        catch_exceptions: bool = True,
255	    ) -> None:
256	        self.charset = charset
257	        self.env: cabc.Mapping[str, str | None] = env or {}
258	        self.echo_stdin = echo_stdin
259	        self.catch_exceptions = catch_exceptions
260	
261	    def get_default_prog_name(self, cli: Command) -> str:
262	        """Given a command object it will return the default program name
263	        for it.  The default is the `name` attribute or ``"root"`` if not
264	        set.
265	        """
266	        return cli.name or "root"
267	
268	    def make_env(
269	        self, overrides: cabc.Mapping[str, str | None] | None = None
270	    ) -> cabc.Mapping[str, str | None]:
271	        """Returns the environment overrides for invoking a script."""
272	        rv = dict(self.env)
273	        if overrides:
274	            rv.update(overrides)
275	        return rv
276	
277	    @contextlib.contextmanager
278	    def isolation(
279	        self,
280	        input: str | bytes | t.IO[t.Any] | None = None,
281	        env: cabc.Mapping[str, str | None] | None = None,
282	        color: bool = False,
283	    ) -> cabc.Iterator[tuple[io.BytesIO, io.BytesIO, io.BytesIO]]:
284	        """A context manager that sets up the isolation for invoking of a
285	        command line tool.  This sets up `<stdin>` with the given input data
286	        and `os.environ` with the overrides from the given dictionary.
287	        This also rebinds some internals in Click to be mocked (like the
288	        prompt functionality).
289	
290	        This is automatically done in the :meth:`invoke` method.
291	
292	        :param input: the input stream to put into `sys.stdin`.
293	        :param env: the environment overrides as dictionary.
294	        :param color: whether the output should contain color codes. The
295	                      application can still override this explicitly.
296	
297	        .. versionadded:: 8.2
298	            An additional output stream is returned, which is a mix of
299	            `<stdout>` and `<stderr>` streams.
300	
301	        .. versionchanged:: 8.2
302	            Always returns the `<stderr>` stream.
303	
304	        .. versionchanged:: 8.0
305	            `<stderr>` is opened with ``errors="backslashreplace"``
306	            instead of the default ``"strict"``.
307	
308	        .. versionchanged:: 4.0
309	            Added the ``color`` parameter.
310	        """
311	        bytes_input = make_input_stream(input, self.charset)
312	        echo_input = None
313	
314	        old_stdin = sys.stdin
315	        old_stdout = sys.stdout
316	        old_stderr = sys.stderr
317	        old_forced_width = formatting.FORCED_WIDTH
318	        formatting.FORCED_WIDTH = 80
319	
320	        env = self.make_env(env)
321	
322	        stream_mixer = StreamMixer()
323	
324	        if self.echo_stdin:
325	            bytes_input = echo_input = t.cast(
326	                t.BinaryIO, EchoingStdin(bytes_input, stream_mixer.stdout)
327	            )
328	
329	        sys.stdin = text_input = _NamedTextIOWrapper(
330	            bytes_input, encoding=self.charset, name="<stdin>", mode="r"
331	        )
332	
333	        if self.echo_stdin:
334	            # Force unbuffered reads, otherwise TextIOWrapper reads a
335	            # large chunk which is echoed early.
336	            text_input._CHUNK_SIZE = 1  # type: ignore
337	
338	        sys.stdout = _NamedTextIOWrapper(
339	            stream_mixer.stdout, encoding=self.charset, name="<stdout>", mode="w"
340	        )
341	
342	        sys.stderr = _NamedTextIOWrapper(
343	            stream_mixer.stderr,
344	            encoding=self.charset,
345	            name="<stderr>",
346	            mode="w",
347	            errors="backslashreplace",
348	        )
349	
350	        @_pause_echo(echo_input)  # type: ignore
351	        def visible_input(prompt: str | None = None) -> str:
352	            sys.stdout.write(prompt or "")
353	            try:
354	                val = next(text_input).rstrip("\r\n")
355	            except StopIteration as e:
356	                raise EOFError() from e
357	            sys.stdout.write(f"{val}\n")
358	            sys.stdout.flush()
359	            return val
360	
361	        @_pause_echo(echo_input)  # type: ignore
362	        def hidden_input(prompt: str | None = None) -> str:
363	            sys.stdout.write(f"{prompt or ''}\n")
364	            sys.stdout.flush()
365	            try:
366	                return next(text_input).rstrip("\r\n")
367	            except StopIteration as e:
368	                raise EOFError() from e
369	
370	        @_pause_echo(echo_input)  # type: ignore
371	        def _getchar(echo: bool) -> str:
372	            char = sys.stdin.read(1)
373	
374	            if echo:
375	                sys.stdout.write(char)
376	
377	            sys.stdout.flush()
378	            return char
379	
380	        default_color = color
381	
382	        def should_strip_ansi(
383	            stream: t.IO[t.Any] | None = None, color: bool | None = None
384	        ) -> bool:
385	            if color is None:
386	                return not default_color
387	            return not color
388	
389	        old_visible_prompt_func = termui.visible_prompt_func
390	        old_hidden_prompt_func = termui.hidden_prompt_func
391	        old__getchar_func = termui._getchar
392	        old_should_strip_ansi = utils.should_strip_ansi  # type: ignore
393	        old__compat_should_strip_ansi = _compat.should_strip_ansi
394	        old_pdb_init = pdb.Pdb.__init__
395	        termui.visible_prompt_func = visible_input
396	        termui.hidden_prompt_func = hidden_input
397	        termui._getchar = _getchar
398	        utils.should_strip_ansi = should_strip_ansi  # type: ignore
399	        _compat.should_strip_ansi = should_strip_ansi
400	
401	        def _patched_pdb_init(
402	            self: pdb.Pdb,
403	            completekey: str = "tab",
404	            stdin: t.IO[str] | None = None,
405	            stdout: t.IO[str] | None = None,
406	            **kwargs: t.Any,
407	        ) -> None:
408	            """Default ``pdb.Pdb`` to real terminal streams during
409	            ``CliRunner`` isolation.
410	
411	            Without this patch, ``pdb.Pdb.__init__`` inherits from
412	            ``cmd.Cmd`` which falls back to ``sys.stdin``/``sys.stdout``
413	            when no explicit streams are provided. During isolation
414	            those are ``BytesIO``-backed wrappers, so the debugger
415	            reads from an empty buffer and writes to captured output,
416	            making interactive debugging impossible.
417	
418	            By defaulting to ``sys.__stdin__``/``sys.__stdout__`` (the
419	            original terminal streams Python preserves regardless of
420	            redirection), debuggers can interact with the user while
421	            ``click.echo`` output is still captured normally.
422	
423	            This covers ``pdb.set_trace()``, ``breakpoint()``,
424	            ``pdb.post_mortem()``, and debuggers that subclass
425	            ``pdb.Pdb`` (ipdb, pdbpp). Explicit ``stdin``/``stdout``
426	            arguments are honored and not overridden. Debuggers that
427	            do not subclass ``pdb.Pdb`` (pudb, debugpy) are not
428	            covered.
429	
430	            See: https://github.com/pallets/click/issues/654 and
431	            https://github.com/pallets/click/issues/824
432	            """
433	            if stdin is None:
434	                stdin = sys.__stdin__
435	            if stdout is None:
436	                stdout = sys.__stdout__
437	            old_pdb_init(
438	                self, completekey=completekey, stdin=stdin, stdout=stdout, **kwargs
439	            )
440	
441	        pdb.Pdb.__init__ = _patched_pdb_init  # type: ignore[assignment]
442	
443	        old_env = {}
444	        try:
445	            for key, value in env.items():
446	                old_env[key] = os.environ.get(key)
447	                if value is None:
448	                    try:
449	                        del os.environ[key]
450	                    except Exception:
451	                        pass
452	                else:
453	                    os.environ[key] = value
454	            yield (stream_mixer.stdout, stream_mixer.stderr, stream_mixer.output)
455	        finally:
456	            for key, value in old_env.items():
457	                if value is None:
458	                    try:
459	                        del os.environ[key]
460	                    except Exception:
461	                        pass
462	                else:
463	                    os.environ[key] = value
464	            sys.stdout = old_stdout
465	            sys.stderr = old_stderr
466	            sys.stdin = old_stdin
467	            termui.visible_prompt_func = old_visible_prompt_func
468	            termui.hidden_prompt_func = old_hidden_prompt_func
469	            termui._getchar = old__getchar_func
470	            utils.should_strip_ansi = old_should_strip_ansi  # type: ignore
471	            _compat.should_strip_ansi = old__compat_should_strip_ansi
472	            formatting.FORCED_WIDTH = old_forced_width
473	            pdb.Pdb.__init__ = old_pdb_init  # type: ignore[method-assign]
474	
475	    def invoke(
476	        self,
477	        cli: Command,
478	        args: str | cabc.Sequence[str] | None = None,
479	        input: str | bytes | t.IO[t.Any] | None = None,
480	        env: cabc.Mapping[str, str | None] | None = None,
481	        catch_exceptions: bool | None = None,
482	        color: bool = False,
483	        **extra: t.Any,
484	    ) -> Result:
485	        """Invokes a command in an isolated environment.  The arguments are
486	        forwarded directly to the command line script, the `extra` keyword
487	        arguments are passed to the :meth:`~clickpkg.Command.main` function of
488	        the command.
489	
490	        This returns a :class:`Result` object.
491	
492	        :param cli: the command to invoke
493	        :param args: the arguments to invoke. It may be given as an iterable
494	                     or a string. When given as string it will be interpreted
495	                     as a Unix shell command. More details at
496	                     :func:`shlex.split`.
497	        :param input: the input data for `sys.stdin`.
498	        :param env: the environment overrides.
499	        :param catch_exceptions: Whether to catch any other exceptions than
500	                                 ``SystemExit``. If :data:`None`, the value
501	                                 from :class:`CliRunner` is used.
502	        :param extra: the keyword arguments to pass to :meth:`main`.
503	        :param color: whether the output should contain color codes. The
504	                      application can still override this explicitly.
505	
506	        .. versionadded:: 8.2
507	            The result object has the ``output_bytes`` attribute with
508	            the mix of ``stdout_bytes`` and ``stderr_bytes``, as the user would
509	            see it in its terminal.
510	
511	        .. versionchanged:: 8.2
512	            The result object always returns the ``stderr_bytes`` stream.
513	
514	        .. versionchanged:: 8.0
515	            The result object has the ``return_value`` attribute with
516	            the value returned from the invoked command.
517	
518	        .. versionchanged:: 4.0
519	            Added the ``color`` parameter.
520	
521	        .. versionchanged:: 3.0
522	            Added the ``catch_exceptions`` parameter.
523	
524	        .. versionchanged:: 3.0
525	            The result object has the ``exc_info`` attribute with the
526	            traceback if available.
527	        """
528	        exc_info = None
529	        if catch_exceptions is None:
530	            catch_exceptions = self.catch_exceptions
531	
532	        with self.isolation(input=input, env=env, color=color) as outstreams:
533	            return_value = None
534	            exception: BaseException | None = None
535	            exit_code = 0
536	
537	            if isinstance(args, str):
538	                args = shlex.split(args)
539	
540	            try:
541	                prog_name = extra.pop("prog_name")
542	            except KeyError:
543	                prog_name = self.get_default_prog_name(cli)
544	
545	            try:
546	                return_value = cli.main(args=args or (), prog_name=prog_name, **extra)
547	            except SystemExit as e:
548	                exc_info = sys.exc_info()
549	                e_code = t.cast("int | t.Any | None", e.code)
550	
551	                if e_code is None:
552	                    e_code = 0
553	
554	                if e_code != 0:
555	                    exception = e
556	
557	                if not isinstance(e_code, int):
558	                    sys.stdout.write(str(e_code))
559	                    sys.stdout.write("\n")
560	                    e_code = 1
561	
562	                exit_code = e_code
563	
564	            except Exception as e:
565	                if not catch_exceptions:
566	                    raise
567	                exception = e
568	                exit_code = 1
569	                exc_info = sys.exc_info()
570	            finally:
571	                sys.stdout.flush()
572	                sys.stderr.flush()
573	                stdout = outstreams[0].getvalue()
574	                stderr = outstreams[1].getvalue()
575	                output = outstreams[2].getvalue()
576	
577	        return Result(
578	            runner=self,
579	            stdout_bytes=stdout,
580	            stderr_bytes=stderr,
581	            output_bytes=output,
582	            return_value=return_value,
583	            exit_code=exit_code,
584	            exception=exception,
585	            exc_info=exc_info,  # type: ignore
586	        )

588	    @contextlib.contextmanager
589	    def isolated_filesystem(
590	        self, temp_dir: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None
591	    ) -> cabc.Iterator[str]:
592	        """A context manager that creates a temporary directory and
593	        changes the current working directory to it. This isolates tests
594	        that affect the contents of the CWD to prevent them from
595	        interfering with each other.
596	
597	        :param temp_dir: Create the temporary directory under this
598	            directory. If given, the created directory is not removed
599	            when exiting.
600	
601	        .. versionchanged:: 8.0
602	            Added the ``temp_dir`` parameter.
603	        """
604	        cwd = os.getcwd()
605	        dt = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=temp_dir)
606	        os.chdir(dt)
607	
608	        try:
609	            yield dt
610	        finally:
611	            os.chdir(cwd)
612	
613	            if temp_dir is None:
614	                import shutil
615	
616	                try:
617	                    shutil.rmtree(dt)
618	                except OSError:
619	                    pass

from __future__ import annotations

import collections.abc as cabc
import contextlib
import io
import os
import pdb
import shlex
import sys
import tempfile
import typing as t
from types import TracebackType

from . import _compat
from . import formatting
from . import termui
from . import utils
from ._compat import _find_binary_reader

if t.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from _typeshed import ReadableBuffer

    from .core import Command


class EchoingStdin:
    def __init__(self, input: t.BinaryIO, output: t.BinaryIO) -> None:
        self._input = input
        self._output = output
        self._paused = False

    def __getattr__(self, x: str) -> t.Any:
        return getattr(self._input, x)

    def _echo(self, rv: bytes) -> bytes:
        if not self._paused:
            self._output.write(rv)

        return rv

    def read(self, n: int = -1) -> bytes:
        return self._echo(self._input.read(n))

    def read1(self, n: int = -1) -> bytes:
        return self._echo(self._input.read1(n))  # type: ignore

    def readline(self, n: int = -1) -> bytes:
        return self._echo(self._input.readline(n))

    def readlines(self) -> list[bytes]:
        return [self._echo(x) for x in self._input.readlines()]

    def __iter__(self) -> cabc.Iterator[bytes]:
        return iter(self._echo(x) for x in self._input)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return repr(self._input)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _pause_echo(stream: EchoingStdin | None) -> cabc.Iterator[None]:
    if stream is None:
        yield
    else:

def make_input_stream(
    input: str | bytes | t.IO[t.Any] | None, charset: str
) -> t.BinaryIO:
    # Is already an input stream.
    if hasattr(input, "read"):

        user would see  it in its terminal.

        runner: CliRunner,
        stdout_bytes: bytes,
        stderr_bytes: bytes,
        output_bytes: bytes,
        return_value: t.Any,
        exit_code: int,
        exception: BaseException | None,
        exc_info: tuple[type[BaseException], BaseException, TracebackType]
        | None = None,

        self.stdout_bytes = stdout_bytes
        self.stderr_bytes = stderr_bytes
        self.output_bytes = output_bytes

            "\r\n", "\n"
        )

    def stdout(self) -> str:

        return self.stdout_bytes.decode(self.runner.charset, "replace").replace(
            "\r\n", "\n"

        self,
        runner: CliRunner,
        stdout_bytes: bytes,
        stderr_bytes: bytes,
        output_bytes: bytes,
        return_value: t.Any,
        exit_code: int,
        exception: BaseException | None,
        exc_info: tuple[type[BaseException], BaseException, TracebackType]
        | None = None,
    ):

        self.stdout_bytes = stdout_bytes
        self.stderr_bytes = stderr_bytes
        self.output_bytes = output_bytes

        self.exit_code = exit_code

        return self.stdout_bytes.decode(self.runner.charset, "replace").replace(

            the value returned from the invoked command.

            Added the ``color`` parameter.

        .. versionchanged:: 3.0

            The result object has the ``exc_info`` attribute with the
            traceback if available.

            catch_exceptions = self.catch_exceptions

            return_value = None
            exception: BaseException | None = None
            exit_code = 0

                e_code = t.cast("int | t.Any | None", e.code)

            runner=self,

class EchoingStdin:
    def __init__(self, input: t.BinaryIO, output: t.BinaryIO) -> None:
        self._input = input
        self._output = output
        self._paused = False

    def __getattr__(self, x: str) -> t.Any:
        return getattr(self._input, x)

    def _echo(self, rv: bytes) -> bytes:
        if not self._paused:
            self._output.write(rv)

        return rv

    def read(self, n: int = -1) -> bytes:
        return self._echo(self._input.read(n))

    def read1(self, n: int = -1) -> bytes:
        return self._echo(self._input.read1(n))  # type: ignore

    def readline(self, n: int = -1) -> bytes:
        return self._echo(self._input.readline(n))

    def readlines(self) -> list[bytes]:
        return [self._echo(x) for x in self._input.readlines()]

    def __iter__(self) -> cabc.Iterator[bytes]:
        return iter(self._echo(x) for x in self._input)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return repr(self._input)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _pause_echo(stream: EchoingStdin | None) -> cabc.Iterator[None]:
    if stream is None:
        yield
    else:
        stream._paused = True
        yield
        stream._paused = False


class BytesIOCopy(tempfile.SpooledTemporaryFile):
    """A ``BytesIO``-like stream that lets the written data be copied to
    another stream.

    Backed by a :class:`tempfile.SpooledTemporaryFile` so that, unlike a
    plain ``io.BytesIO``, it exposes a real file descriptor through
    ``fileno()``. This allows the stream to be used as ``stdout``/``stderr``
    for :class:`subprocess.Popen` (and :func:`subprocess.run`) while under
    :class:`CliRunner` isolation.

    .. versionadded:: 8.2
    """

    def __init__(self, copy_to: io.BytesIO) -> None:
        super().__init__(mode="wb+")
        self.copy_to = copy_to

    def flush(self) -> None:
        super().flush()
        self.copy_to.flush()

    def write(self, b: ReadableBuffer) -> int:
        self.copy_to.write(b)
        return super().write(b)

    def getvalue(self) -> bytes:
        pos = self.tell()
        try:
            self.seek(0)
            return self.read()
        finally:
            self.seek(pos)


class StreamMixer:
    """Mixes `<stdout>` and `<stderr>` streams.

    The result is available in the ``output`` attribute.

    .. versionadded:: 8.2
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.output: io.BytesIO = io.BytesIO()
        self.stdout: io.BytesIO = BytesIOCopy(copy_to=self.output)
        self.stderr: io.BytesIO = BytesIOCopy(copy_to=self.output)


class _NamedTextIOWrapper(io.TextIOWrapper):
    def __init__(

    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(buffer, **kwargs)

    def close(self) -> None:

        prevent the default __del__ implementation from closing that buffer.

        .. versionadded:: 8.3.2
        """
        ...

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:

    @property

def make_input_stream(
    input: str | bytes | t.IO[t.Any] | None, charset: str
) -> t.BinaryIO:
    # Is already an input stream.
    if hasattr(input, "read"):
        rv = _find_binary_reader(t.cast("t.IO[t.Any]", input))

        if rv is not None:
            return rv

        raise TypeError("Could not find binary reader for input stream.")

    if input is None:
        input = b""
    elif isinstance(input, str):
        input = input.encode(charset)

    return io.BytesIO(input)


class Result:
    """Holds the captured result of an invoked CLI script.

    :param runner: The runner that created the result
    :param stdout_bytes: The standard output as bytes.
    :param stderr_bytes: The standard error as bytes.
    :param output_bytes: A mix of ``stdout_bytes`` and ``stderr_bytes``, as the
        user would see  it in its terminal.
    :param return_value: The value returned from the invoked command.
    :param exit_code: The exit code as integer.
    :param exception: The exception that happened if one did.
    :param exc_info: Exception information (exception type, exception instance,
        traceback type).

    .. versionchanged:: 8.2
        ``stderr_bytes`` no longer optional, ``output_bytes`` introduced and
        ``mix_stderr`` has been removed.

    .. versionadded:: 8.0
        Added ``return_value``.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        runner: CliRunner,
        stdout_bytes: bytes,
        stderr_bytes: bytes,
        output_bytes: bytes,
        return_value: t.Any,
        exit_code: int,
        exception: BaseException | None,
        exc_info: tuple[type[BaseException], BaseException, TracebackType]
        | None = None,
    ):
        self.runner = runner
        self.stdout_bytes = stdout_bytes
        self.stderr_bytes = stderr_bytes
        self.output_bytes = output_bytes
        self.return_value = return_value
        self.exit_code = exit_code
        self.exception = exception
        self.exc_info = exc_info

    @property
    def output(self) -> str:
        """The terminal output as unicode string, as the user would see it.

        .. versionchanged:: 8.2
            No longer a proxy for ``self.stdout``. Now has its own independent stream
            that is mixing `<stdout>` and `<stderr>`, in the order they were written.
        """
        return self.output_bytes.decode(self.runner.charset, "replace").replace(
            "\r\n", "\n"
        )

    @property
    def stdout(self) -> str:
        """The standard output as unicode string."""
        return self.stdout_bytes.decode(self.runner.charset, "replace").replace(
            "\r\n", "\n"
        )

    @property
    def stderr(self) -> str:
        """The standard error as unicode string.

        .. versionchanged:: 8.2
            No longer raise an exception, always returns the `<stderr>` string.
        """
        return self.stderr_bytes.decode(self.runner.charset, "replace").replace(
            "\r\n", "\n"
        )

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        exc_str = repr(self.exception) if self.exception else "okay"
        return f"<{type(self).__name__} {exc_str}>"

    script for unittesting purposes in a isolated environment.  This only
    works in single-threaded systems without any concurrency as it changes the
    global interpreter state.

    :param charset: the character set for the input and output data.
    :param env: a dictionary with environment variables for overriding.
    :param echo_stdin: if this is set to `True`, then reading from `<stdin>` writes
                       to `<stdout>`.  This is useful for showing examples in
                       some circumstances.  Note that regular prompts
                       will automatically echo the input.
    :param catch_exceptions: Whether to catch any exceptions other than
                             ``SystemExit`` when running :meth:`~CliRunner.invoke`.

    .. versionchanged:: 8.2
        Added the ``catch_exceptions`` parameter.

    .. versionchanged:: 8.2
        ``mix_stderr`` parameter has been removed.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        charset: str = "utf-8",
        env: cabc.Mapping[str, str | None] | None = None,
        echo_stdin: bool = False,
        catch_exceptions: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        self.charset = charset
        self.env: cabc.Mapping[str, str | None] = env or {}
        self.echo_stdin = echo_stdin
        self.catch_exceptions = catch_exceptions

    def get_default_prog_name(self, cli: Command) -> str:
        """Given a command object it will return the default program name
        for it.  The default is the `name` attribute or ``"root"`` if not
        set.
        """
        return cli.name or "root"

    def make_env(
        self, overrides: cabc.Mapping[str, str | None] | None = None
    ) -> cabc.Mapping[str, str | None]:
        """Returns the environment overrides for invoking a script."""
        rv = dict(self.env)
        if overrides:
            rv.update(overrides)
        return rv

    @contextlib.contextmanager
    def isolation(
        self,
        input: str | bytes | t.IO[t.Any] | None = None,
        env: cabc.Mapping[str, str | None] | None = None,
        color: bool = False,
    ) -> cabc.Iterator[tuple[io.BytesIO, io.BytesIO, io.BytesIO]]:
        """A context manager that sets up the isolation for invoking of a
        command line tool.  This sets up `<stdin>` with the given input data
        and `os.environ` with the overrides from the given dictionary.
        This also rebinds some internals in Click to be mocked (like the
        prompt functionality).

        This is automatically done in the :meth:`invoke` method.

        :param input: the input stream to put into `sys.stdin`.
        :param env: the environment overrides as dictionary.
        :param color: whether the output should contain color codes. The
                      application can still override this explicitly.

        .. versionadded:: 8.2
            An additional output stream is returned, which is a mix of
            `<stdout>` and `<stderr>` streams.

        .. versionchanged:: 8.2
            Always returns the `<stderr>` stream.

        .. versionchanged:: 8.0
            `<stderr>` is opened with ``errors="backslashreplace"``
            instead of the default ``"strict"``.

        .. versionchanged:: 4.0
            Added the ``color`` parameter.
        """
        bytes_input = make_input_stream(input, self.charset)
        echo_input = None

        old_stdin = sys.stdin
        old_stdout = sys.stdout
        old_stderr = sys.stderr
        old_forced_width = formatting.FORCED_WIDTH
        formatting.FORCED_WIDTH = 80

        env = self.make_env(env)

        stream_mixer = StreamMixer()

        if self.echo_stdin:
            bytes_input = echo_input = t.cast(
                t.BinaryIO, EchoingStdin(bytes_input, stream_mixer.stdout)
            )

        sys.stdin = text_input = _NamedTextIOWrapper(
            bytes_input, encoding=self.charset, name="<stdin>", mode="r"
        )

        if self.echo_stdin:

            # large chunk which is echoed early.
            text_input._CHUNK_SIZE = 1  # type: ignore

        sys.stdout = _NamedTextIOWrapper(
            stream_mixer.stdout, encoding=self.charset, name="<stdout>", mode="w"
        )

        sys.stderr = _NamedTextIOWrapper(
            stream_mixer.stderr,
            encoding=self.charset,
            name="<stderr>",
            mode="w",
            errors="backslashreplace",
        )

        @_pause_echo(echo_input)  # type: ignore
        def visible_input(prompt: str | None = None) -> str:
            sys.stdout.write(prompt or "")
            try:
                val = next(text_input).rstrip("\r\n")
            except StopIteration as e:
                raise EOFError() from e
            sys.stdout.write(f"{val}\n")
            sys.stdout.flush()
            return val

        @_pause_echo(echo_input)  # type: ignore
        def hidden_input(prompt: str | None = None) -> str:
            sys.stdout.write(f"{prompt or ''}\n")
            sys.stdout.flush()
            try:
                return next(text_input).rstrip("\r\n")
            except StopIteration as e:
                raise EOFError() from e

        @_pause_echo(echo_input)  # type: ignore
        def _getchar(echo: bool) -> str:
            char = sys.stdin.read(1)

            if echo:
                sys.stdout.write(char)

            sys.stdout.flush()
            return char

            stream: t.IO[t.Any] | None = None, color: bool | None = None

            if color is None:

            return not color

        old_hidden_prompt_func = termui.hidden_prompt_func
        old__getchar_func = termui._getchar
        old_should_strip_ansi = utils.should_strip_ansi  # type: ignore
        old__compat_should_strip_ansi = _compat.should_strip_ansi
        old_pdb_init = pdb.Pdb.__init__
        termui.visible_prompt_func = visible_input
        termui.hidden_prompt_func = hidden_input
        termui._getchar = _getchar

        def _patched_pdb_init(
            self: pdb.Pdb,

            https://github.com/pallets/click/issues/824

class EchoingStdin:
    def __init__(self, input: t.BinaryIO, output: t.BinaryIO) -> None:
        self._input = input
        self._output = output
        self._paused = False

    def __getattr__(self, x: str) -> t.Any:
        return getattr(self._input, x)

    def _echo(self, rv: bytes) -> bytes:
        if not self._paused:
            self._output.write(rv)

        return rv

    def read(self, n: int = -1) -> bytes:
        return self._echo(self._input.read(n))

    def read1(self, n: int = -1) -> bytes:
        return self._echo(self._input.read1(n))  # type: ignore

    def readline(self, n: int = -1) -> bytes:
        return self._echo(self._input.readline(n))

    def readlines(self) -> list[bytes]:
        return [self._echo(x) for x in self._input.readlines()]

    def __iter__(self) -> cabc.Iterator[bytes]:
        return iter(self._echo(x) for x in self._input)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return repr(self._input)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _pause_echo(stream: EchoingStdin | None) -> cabc.Iterator[None]:
    if stream is None:
        yield
    else:
        stream._paused = True
        yield
        stream._paused = False


class BytesIOCopy(tempfile.SpooledTemporaryFile):
    """A ``BytesIO``-like stream that lets the written data be copied to
    another stream.

    Backed by a :class:`tempfile.SpooledTemporaryFile` so that, unlike a
    plain ``io.BytesIO``, it exposes a real file descriptor through
    ``fileno()``. This allows the stream to be used as ``stdout``/``stderr``
    for :class:`subprocess.Popen` (and :func:`subprocess.run`) while under
    :class:`CliRunner` isolation.

    .. versionadded:: 8.2
    """

    def __init__(self, copy_to: io.BytesIO) -> None:
        super().__init__(mode="wb+")
        self.copy_to = copy_to

    def flush(self) -> None:
        super().flush()
        self.copy_to.flush()

    def write(self, b: ReadableBuffer) -> int:
        self.copy_to.write(b)
        return super().write(b)

    def getvalue(self) -> bytes:
        pos = self.tell()
        try:
            self.seek(0)
            return self.read()
        finally:
            self.seek(pos)

    """Mixes `<stdout>` and `<stderr>` streams.

        self.stdout: io.BytesIO = BytesIOCopy(copy_to=self.output)
        self.stderr: io.BytesIO = BytesIOCopy(copy_to=self.output)

## Summary

Fixed `src/click/testing.py`: `CliRunner`'s `BytesIOCopy` (the buffer backing `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` under isolation) was a plain `io.BytesIO`, which raises `io.UnsupportedOperation` on `fileno()`. This broke any code invoked via `CliRunner.invoke()` that passed `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` to `subprocess.run`/`Popen` (which needs a real file descriptor).

`BytesIOCopy` now lazily materializes a real, file-descriptor-backed temporary file the first time `fileno()` is called, transferring the buffered content to it and delegating subsequent reads/writes there.
